texts.preamble: Rupam Sharm vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 September, 2025 Author: Milind Ramesh Phadke Bench: Milind Ramesh Phadke Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:20642 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke On The 3 rd Of September, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 4867 of 2015 Rupam Sharm Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance: Shri Satyendra Singh Rajput and Shri Sanjay Bahirani - Ad petitioner. Shri Samar Ghuraiya - Public Prosecutor for the State. Order The petitioner has approached this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, challenging the order dated 21.04.2015 passed by the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Guna, in Criminal Case No.1388 of 2009.
texts.facts: Order The petitioner has approached this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, challenging the order dated 21.04.2015 passed by the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Guna, in Criminal Case No.1388 of 2009. By way of present petition, the petitioner has made following prayer: 1) This present criminal petition may kindly be allowed; and 2) The Criminal Case No. 1388/2009 which is pending before the court of JMFC, (Shri Sachin Jain), Guna be [LEAKAGE_MASK]; and 3) The offence U/s. 2(i)7(i) of the prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and 50(i) R/w. U/s. 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules pending before the JMFC, Guna be [LEAKAGE_MASK]; and 4) The, any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deem fit in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20642 Rupam Sharm vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171195682/ 1 2 MCRC-4867-2015 the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be issued doing justice in the matter." The petitioner faces prosecution under Section 2(i) and 7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, read with Section 50(i) and Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, based on a complaint filed by Smt. Bhavna Thakur, Food Inspector, on behalf of the State. The complaint alleges that the milk sold by the petitioner was adulterated. The milk sample in question was allegedly collected by the complainant on 29.11.2007. However, the complaint was filed before the learned CJM, Guna, only on 25.06.2009, after a considerable delay of more than seven months from the date of sample collection and after the expiry of the shelf life of the milk. The complainant sent the milk sample for testing to the State Food Laboratory (SFL) on 03.01.2008, and it was received on 11.01.2008. The delay in filing the complaint and the timeline for testing do not justify the prosecution against the petitioner. The complainant further filed an application for testing the sample before the Central Food Laboratory (CFL) on 08.07.2009, which was allowed by the learned trial court; however, the CFL report has never been received despite repeated follow-ups. The learned trial court framed charges against the petitioner without receipt of the CFL report. Evidence of both parties was thereafter recorded, and the matter was fixed for final arguments. Prior to the pronouncement of judgment, the complainant filed an application on 13.03.2015 for retesting of a third sample of the milk. The petitioner filed a reply opposing the application, submitting that the original sample was collected on 29.11.2007 and Section 13(2C) of the Act provides for retesting a third sample only if the earlier sample sent to the CFL was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20642 3 MCRC-4867-2015 lost or damaged, but the complainant has made no claim that the earlier sample was lost or damaged. The application for retesting has been filed after a lapse of almost eight years, which is wholly unjustified and prejudicial to the petitioner. Despite these objections, the learned trial court allowed the application for retesting of the third sample, which is illegal. texts.arguments: Section 13(2C) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, stipulates that "Where two parts of the sample have been sent to the court and only one part of the sample has been sent by the court to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory under sub-section (2B), the court shall, as soon as practicable, return the remaining part to the Local (Health) Authority and that Authority shall destroy that part after the certificate from the Director of the Central Food Laboratory has been received by the court." The proviso to this section further provides that if the part of the sample sent by the court to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory is lost or damaged, the court shall require the Local (Health) Authority to forward the part of the sample, if any, retained by it to the court and on receipt thereof, the court shall proceed in the manner provided in sub-section (2B). In the case of M/s Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt. Ltd v. State of Maharashtra (2024), the Bombay High Court observed that the accused did not avail the remedy for a second analysis under the Food and Adulteration Act and therefore, no opportunity was granted to them. Similarly, in Daljeet Singh v. State of U.P. (2025), the Allahabad High Court dealt with issues related to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20642 4 MCRC-4867-2015 compliance of provisions of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
